messages:
jeff_corp: Hey, embeddings started returning a different vector width after we pinned a model yesterday. We used to get 1536 floats, now it's 1024. Breaking our index.
lee_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the request + a small snippet of the response? Also which model id/variant did you pin?
jeff_corp: Here ya go:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-alpha:2026-03-10-pinned","input":["hello world"]}'
```
response: 
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001,0.002,...],"usage":{} }],"model":"open-embed-alpha:2026-03-10-pinned"}
```
(embedding length reported by our code: 1024)
lee_support: Thanks. Can you confirm your previous vectors were 1536 from the same model name before pinning?
jeff_corp: Yes, same model name (we had been using open-embed-alpha:latest for months, then pinned to the timestamp above to avoid drift).
maria_se: Quick note: there was a canary rollout last week where an experimental "compact" embed variant (1024 dims) was introduced as a cost experiment. We expect it only on the "-compact" variant, but I'll check routing rules.
infra-bot: deploy-router: 2026-03-10T03:42:11Z route update applied: open-embed-alpha -> variant fallback order [open-embed-alpha-v2-1536, open-embed-alpha-compact-1024]
lee_support: Hmm the router log shows fallback order that could pick compact if the pinned variant didn't map. Can you send the exact pin payload you used?
jeff_corp: We used the Console pin: model=open-embed-alpha, pinned_to=2026-03-10. I don't have the raw API for pinning.
maria_se: Could be that the pin resolved to a variant alias that maps to compact. I'll ask runtime to verify the model artifact dimension meta. @nina_eng can you check model metadata and any alias shims?
nina_eng: On it. Querying model catalog...
nina_eng: catalog-get: open-embed-alpha:2026-03-10 meta.embedding_dim = "1024"
nina_eng: Looks like the artifact published at that tag is a compact build (1024). The latest live alias (latest) still points to 1536 variant.
lee_support: That explains it — your pin anchored you to a different artifact than you expected. Two paths: 1) unpin / repin to the 1536 artifact id; 2) re-encode/reindex on your side to 1024. We can assist with both.
jeff_corp: How did this happen? The Console pin tool showed the same model name as before.
maria_se: The Console uses human-friendly tags (date-based) that can map to different internal artifact builds if someone republished the date tag. We'll add clearer artifact checks.
lee_support: For immediate mitigation, we can create a compatibility guard that rejects pin operations if embedding_dim != previously seen dim for the customer's namespace. Want us to enable that on your org?
jeff_corp: Yes please, that would be helpful to avoid silent breaks.
lee_support: While we do that, can you run a quick check to confirm all existing stored vectors are 1536? If yes, we'll help you repin to the 1536 artifact or provide a one-off migration job.
jeff_corp: Confirmed: index vectors are 1536. We'd prefer a hotfix to keep service stable and then a migration later.
infra-bot: ticket-create: #INC-2026-891 created and assigned to eng-runtime with priority P1 — subject: pinned model resolution produced different embedding_dim for customer jeff_corp
lee_support: I've attached your thread to INC-2026-891. Engineers will look at artifact mapping and pin behavior.
maria_se: Temporary plan: set org-level pin-guard to block pins that change embedding dim, and add a console modal showing artifact digest and dim before pin confirm.
nina_eng: Also adding server-side validation to the embeddings endpoint: if requesting a pinned model and its declared embedding_dim differs from previous usage metadata for that org, return 409 with guidance. I'll draft the change.
jeff_corp: Thanks — any ETA?
lee_support: We enabled the org pin-guard flag for you at 2026-03-10T06:10Z (disabled for others). ENG expects a patch to runtime by EOD UTC and a console UX patch in the next release.
ops_oncall: Oncall noted. If you want us to temporarily repin you to a 1536 artifact, provide the artifact id and we'll do a safe swap with a canary verification.
jeff_corp: Please do that. Artifact id for the 1536 build is sha256:abcd1234ef...
lee_support: Kicking the repin now, will run quick sanity test against a sample of your requests.
infra-bot: deploy-router: 2026-03-10T06:35:12Z update: org-pin override applied for org=jeff_corp -> artifact sha256:abcd1234ef... verified
nina_eng: Verified: your subsequent embedding calls return 1536 dims again. Please run your index validation.
jeff_corp: Verified — indexing resumed. Big thanks.
lee_support: Follow-ups: (1) ENG will add pin-dim-guard globally; (2) Console will surface artifact digest + dim before pin commit; (3) we documented workaround steps for customers. We'll keep INC-2026-891 open until TODOs complete.
maria_se: Adding notes to the release checklist to prevent date-tag republishing without immutable digest change logs. :memo:
jeff_corp: Appreciate the fast help. :heart:
lee_support: Glad it's fixed. Reopen here if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:
